implementation.replacementStatus: partial; element animation APIs built, full renderer pending
implementation.targetScope: Independent numeric and CSS-unit element animation APIs, DOM reads/keyframe resolution, MotionValue transitions, DOM effects, tween/spring playback, values, scheduling and mapping. Not a drop-in replacement for motion-dom yet.
implementation.remainingWork: Custom effect registration, VisualElement handoff, transitionEnd and high-level selector/group animate wrapper; complex none/color/string keyframes, arbitrary multi-axis 3D decomposition, inertia and grid/random stagger; WAAPI, gestures/layout and full unchanged Framer Motion caller acceptance. CSS spring serialization is not implemented. Remaining runtime is unimplemented, not retained upstream code.

independentComponents.numeric interpolation: Snapshot ranges, binary lookup, custom mixers and per-segment easing
independentComponents.MotionValue: State, velocity, mutation-safe subscriptions, passive effects and owned external-animation lifecycle
independentComponents.frame scheduling: Eight ordered phases, dedupe/cancellation/keep-alive, microtasks and manual frame processing
independentComponents.numeric playback: Owned numeric keyframes, offsets and easing; millisecond generators and tween controllers with delays, repeats, seeking, speed, pause/resume and lifecycle cleanup
independentComponents.spring playback: Analytic under/critical/overdamped oscillator, velocity and retargeting; duration/visual-duration calibration; bounded settling estimates and playback integration
independentComponents.DOM effects: Deferred and coalesced style/attribute/property/SVG bindings, unit-aware transform composition, path drawing, selectors, scoped flush/release and cleanup ownership
independentComponents.numeric transition adapters: Seconds-based animateMotionValue, property defaults/overrides, owned keyframe wildcards/options and current velocity integration
independentComponents.element reads and resolution: Owner-document CSS/SVG reads, matrix extraction, bounded variable fallbacks, owned keyframes, cancellation/resume, grouped layout measurement and transactional style restoration
independentComponents.single-value animation: Public animateSingleValue entry for numeric scalars and MotionValues; validates replacements before stopping existing playback and preserves lifecycle errors through finished
independentComponents.element animation: animateElement and animateValues connect owned values, deferred DOM keyframe resolution, numeric controllers and shared HTML/SVG effects; public controls use seconds including delay.

changes: No upstream runtime copied; depends only on vmotion-utils.
Owns range and easing-array snapshots; rejects malformed ranges before animation starts.
Binary segment lookup bounds the cost of long numeric timelines.
Cancellation suppresses callbacks already queued in the active phase. Callback failures release processing state and allow remaining work and future frames to proceed.

Synchronous animation completion reports start before completion; late completion after cancellation does not emit a success event. Failed start hooks and throwing stop handlers release owned resources.
MotionValue retains vmotion-utils subscription lifetime protections and stops unobserved animations on the next frame, allowing same-frame resubscription.
Reversing delayed playback preserves the current value instead of reapplying a signed delay and jumping.
Paused animations release their frame callback; explicit seek, completion and cancellation apply values immediately, and callback failures clean up driver ownership.
Standalone visualDuration is honored rather than silently ignored without a bounce option.
Settled spring repeat gaps retain the endpoint; invalid retarget operations preserve the previous trajectory.
Direct element effects work across document/window boundaries; both controls silently skip a directly supplied iframe element.

Binding maps validate before attachment, stale cleanup cannot detach replacements, and queued writes are suppressed after cleanup. Nonfinite numeric styling rejects without losing other writes or future frames.
Avoids unavailable-frame wakeup setup in manual/server timing; composes transforms directly from owned binding slots without per-frame lookup arrays or unit-string helpers.

Numeric transition factories snapshot targets/options and resolve current values at start; updates and completion preserve MotionValue lifecycle ownership. DOM measurement and handoff reject explicitly until implemented.

Rotated 2D scale readings retain magnitude, absent axes return identity defaults, and malformed matrices reject. Matrix decomposition uses a documented canonical convention, not recovery of the original transform function list.

DOM measurement restores owned styles and priorities before callbacks, including on failure; conflicting same-property measurements are isolated. Failed reads/callbacks do not strand unrelated queued work.
Single-value animation validates paused controllers before replacement; start/completion listener failures reject finished, while stop and cancellation settle playback and replays use fresh promises.
Resolver batches preserve any thrown value, including falsy exceptions, and restore window scroll after temporary layout measurements.

Setup owns one prepared option snapshot, creates playback promises only when observed, and caches CSS variable syntax without caching computed values. Resolver cancellation targets its read phase and allocates layout transactions only when needed.

Element animations reject unsupported targets, preserve responsive variable/percentage endpoints, share direct effect values and cancel unresolved work on release. Failed deferred resolution retains prior playback; reentrant replacement cannot reattach stale controllers.

Element controls reuse prepared numeric playback, make completion waiting lazy, and index shared render jobs once per binding. Explicit stop removes a redundant deferred unobserved-value check. Packed tests now route every test file to the installed runtime.

Element setup reuses one internal option snapshot and one lifecycle facade, avoiding duplicate controller/configuration allocations. Public factories and caller arrays remain independently snapshotted. Synchronous start-hook completion does not restart finished playback.

caller.scope: Fade/transform animation and Motion value subscriptions beneath motion/react. Built foundation only; application adoption not claimed.
